standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.npc: Arr? Be ye wantin' te go on account with our gang o' fillibusters?
The powder monkey be takin' a caulk after gettin' rowdy on bumboo, so there be plenty of room for ye.

standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.player: I'll just be over here if you need me.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy.npc: Yer standin' in me light stranger. Can I sell ye somethin' that'll make ye move?

options.text: Probably, let's see what you have.

steps.player: Probably, let's see what you have.

steps.npc: Then move on stranger.

options.text: That depends on if you have any cutlasses.

steps.player: That depends on if you have any cutlasses.

steps.npc: Cutlasses! Think yer a pirate now [lad/lass/kid]?
Well, I have some cutlasses.
I have Brass Hand Harry's Cutlass. Well, a load of them to be honest.
Then there's Unlucky Jenkins' Lucky Cutlass. Lovely blade that.
I've also got Gentleman Mallard's Rapier. Not a cutlass I know, but the finest blade ever wielded by a privateer.
Now, which would ye like to hear about?
A good choice!
Ye may end up meeting Brass Hand Harry if ye hang around long enough.
He lost his left arm to a canister round, but that didn't stop him much.
Then he lost his right hand at the wrist fightin' the excise men off the coast of Karamja.
Not bein' the sort to lie about mopin', he asked me to make him a cutlass with a brass gauntlet fixed to the handle, and rig it up with a load of straps so he could keep fightin'.
He's a great man is Harry, but he keeps snappin' the straps while he's at sea, so he sells the cutlasses back to me in exchange for a new one.
It's quite a good blade, but the big, brass gauntlet is what makes it worthwhile. It's big enough to fit over even a real gauntlet, so ye get extra protection to yer sword hand.
I can sell ye one fer 1040 coins.
Interested?

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 1040 coins:
If the player has at least 1040 coins:

steps.npc: Here ye go. I've got a load of these left over if ye need more.
Arr, tis a sad tale to this sword.
Jenkins was the lookout on the Jonah, a cursed vessel if there ever was one.

One day his ship were attacked by another group of pirates durin' a fierce storm. One of their bowmen took a shot at the Cap'n of the vessel, but it were deflected off his compass and hit Jenkins in the back.
That weren't the worst of it [lad/lass/kid]. He survived the fight, and the ship's surgeon was trying to get the arrow out when...
Are ye familiar with the spell bones to bananas?
Well, due to a blow to the head he took in the fight, the surgeon cast that spell, thinking it was some sort of new healing spell.
And he did so while touching Jenkins' ribs.
No [lad/lass/kid]!
See, he survived, his bones turned to bananas, as a huge storm blew up and the crew debated what to do with him.

But you see, the storm was actually the tail end of a hurricane that had swept the nearby jungle islands, and when it approached the ship it petered out, droppin' all manner of strange things onto the deck and into the
ocean.
The worst part was when the ship was bombarded with ravenous, hunger-crazed monkeys, the majority of which landed on Jenkins as he lay recoverin'.
No [lad/lass/kid]!
See, what happened next, after the monkeys had had their way with him was...

steps.player: Look, I don't want to hear any more. Why would I want to buy his cutlass?

steps.npc: Well, after the poor man passed on...
In a final, terrifying, mashed potato coated tragedy...
His shipmates found his cutlass was completely untouched.
See, having been exposed to all the bad luck that Jenkins went through, the thing is unlikely to ever see anything that bad again.
Hence, it must be lucky.
Ye can have it fer 2560 coins.
Interested?

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 2560 coins:
If the player has at least 2560 coins:

steps.npc: Here ye go. I hope it brings you luck.
Well, I'll tell ye the story, but it'll take a great deal of convincin' for me to sell you this rapier.
See, gentleman Mallard is a legend in these parts. His family had been rich, shipping all sorts of goods up and down the coast.
Then their rivals got together and had their ships sunk, one after the other, and his business partners were all either bought off or had...accidents.
With no money and only one ship left, he took to the life of a pirate, but no brigand was he.
He took only from those men that had brought about his downfall, was fair with his men, and generous with his loot.
Why, this island would have been wiped out by the shakes if he hadn't turned over his stash to buy medicine.
One day his ship was attacked by a huge sea creature that swept the decks of men with its tentacles.
The crew took to the lifeboats, and the last they saw of him the gentleman was stabbin' at the thing as it hauled the ship under the water.
A week later about ten foot of tentacle washed up on the beach, with his rapier embedded in it to the hilt.
I took it, cleaned it up, and I've been lookin' after it ever since.
I can't let it go for less than 25600 coins, and even then that's a bargain.
Ye think ye have what it takes to wield it?

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 25600 coins:
If the player has at least 25600 coins:

steps.npc: I hope yer worthy enough to wield this, stranger. I'd hate te think Gentleman Mallard would be disappointed in me fer sellin' it to ye.

options.text: I have this anchor, can you fix it?
options.condition: If the player has a broken barrelchest anchor in their inventory:

steps.player: I have this anchor, can you fix it?

steps.npc: Well, this is a very unusual job. This thing looks more suited to bashin' peoples heads in than securing a ship.
Where did ye get it?

steps.player: You wouldn't believe me if I told you.

steps.npc: Stole it eh? Well I can sort it out for 230000 coins, if you like.

steps.text: If the player does not have 230,000 coins:

steps.player: That's too much for me at the moment.

steps.npc: Right, let's get to work.
There ye go, good as new!

4nFhAQ.npc: Smart [lad/lass/kid]! Come and see me when ye have the coins fer it.

AgtJY7.npc: Well I'll still be here if ye change yer mind.
